_about: Theme standard, workstream E. 26 accents + 6 rung recipes + 5 states + 7 exceptions; every preset is derived from them. Companion to theme-standard.md. Visual truth is 'Theme Standard - Plates, Beams & Icons.dc.html'.
_rule: A tier block authors exactly two values: accent + rung. Icon, beam and plate are pure functions of those. Presets carry NO FontSize.

rung_recipes._about: T0/T1/T6 are house-fixed in STRUCTURE (white plate + red border; the red T1 plate; the T6 grey) but T0's TEXT is accent.solid — see t0_text_rule. T2-T5 are derived from the accent. 'painted' sets text; 'rarity_through' deliberately omits it so the game paints rarity.

T0.name: Drop everything

rarity_through.note: chase overrides rarity — painted in every family, gear included

T0._border_note: NO border. The border is reserved for state deviations on every rung including T0 — it is the only channel free on every item in every category, which is what makes states composable. T0 is unmistakable from red-on-white alone.

T3.name: Situational / bulk
T3.note: Currency keeps Sharket's tan. Every other category mutes its own accent.

rarity_through.note: bare game default — emit no colour lines at all

_t5_border_rule.what: T5 painted drops its plate: no SetBackgroundColor, dim accent text, dim accent border.
_t5_border_rule.why: It is the floor, so the lightest possible treatment is right — an outline over the game's own background rather than a plate.
_t5_border_rule.constraint: ⚠️ It spends the border, so it is LEGAL ONLY WHERE state_budget IS EMPTY: currency, shards and splinters, fragments, scarabs, divination cards, essences, oils, fossils. The test is mechanical — state_budget[class].length === 0.
_t5_border_rule.everyone_else: Any category with one or more states keeps the 48 48 48 plate at T5 and no border (painted_with_states above). That is gems, jewels, uniques, maps, heist and all equipment.
_t5_border_rule.validator: This is the one place a rung's look depends on the class. Assert it: if state_budget[class] is non-empty and the resolved T5 preset emits SetBorderColor, that is an error.
_t5_border_rule.note: Earlier drafts put this treatment on T2. Reverted — T2 is a solid accent plate again.
_t5_border_rule.gold: Gold is the permanent case: plate: never on its accent, so it takes this form at whatever rung a block puts it on. Everything else takes it only at T5.

_t0_text_rule.answer: (b) — T0 text is accent.solid, plate stays white, border stays 255 0 0.
_t0_text_rule.why: The §04 exception rows are the evidence: Mageblood is 175 96 37 on white, The Doctor 14 186 255, an Awakened gem 27 162 155. The white plate is the house part; the text is the family. The border is neither — it stays free for states.
_t0_text_rule.currency_is_the_exception: 255 170 0 on white is ~1.9:1 — illegible. So accents whose solid fails 4.5:1 on white carry an explicit t0_text. Currency's is 255 0 0 (Sharket's mirror red, which is also T0's border).
_t0_text_rule.contrast_bar: 3:1, not 4.5:1 — your call and it is the right one: T0 ships at 45px, which is large text by any standard. 4.5:1 is unreachable anyway (pure red on white is 4.00:1 by construction, so currency's own t0_text could never pass).
_t0_text_rule.resolution: 14 accents now carry an explicit t0_text — the original 3, the 10 your check caught, and recipes, added with the accent itself. Each is its accent darkened until it clears 3:1 on white, so the family still reads. maps / harvest / expedition were the urgent ones: 1.67:1 is, as you put it, a rumour.
_t0_text_rule.dark_plate_considered: DECLINED, though it was the better engineering answer. A dark T0 plate would let every accent through at full saturation and delete this whole class of problem — but the white plate IS the halo, it is Sharket's mirror look, and with the border unavailable the plate is the only channel T0 has left to distinguish itself from T1's red. Ten authored values is the cheaper price.
_t0_text_rule.keep_uniques: uniques at 4.64:1 is the only accent that clears 4.5 unaided and is already the colour players read as chase. Left alone.

_plate_rule._about: MEASURED FROM NEVERSINK (2026-08-03): their filters hold ONE background per category across ~50 consecutive blocks (47 0 74, 40 0 40, 20 20 0, 0 40 15). They never ramp a hue through four steps. That ruled out my original T2-T5 lightness ramp.
_plate_rule.final_shape: Plate luminance descends TWICE and never doubles back: accent.solid (T2) -> accent.muted (T3) -> house grey 80 (T4) -> house grey 48 (T5). Currency: 176 -> 158 -> 80 -> 48.
_plate_rule.key_move: The accent LEAVES the plate at T4 and survives only as text. That is Sharket's own scroll look, and it is why the bottom of the ladder stops competing with the top.
_plate_rule.ladder_is_six: T0-T5. There is no T6 — the old T6 grey became T5, and Sharket's scroll plate became T4.
_plate_rule.retired: accent.muted_deep, accent lerp(solid,deep,0.72), the per-rung alpha ramp, bg_currency, and the whole T6 row.

_rarity_through_rule._about: CORRECTION to an error I introduced: rarity_through does NOT put the rung on the border.
_rarity_through_rule.why: Gear is the only class that holds all five state borders. If the rung spends the border, the five Continue deviations have nothing to layer onto on exactly the class that needs them. §6's invariant holds without exception: the border is the only channel free on every item in every category.
_rarity_through_rule.how_the_rung_reads_instead: Same hue throughout (accent.deep), ranked by ALPHA — 245 / 240 / 225 / 210 — plus SetFontSize and the icon. Alpha is not a state channel, so nothing competes.
_rarity_through_rule.note: The painted column ranks by text; the rarity_through column ranks by alpha. Both keep one hue and both leave the border alone.
_rarity_through_rule.it_is_an_accent_property: rarity_through is declared ONCE, on the accent, and is never a per-row choice. Only equipment has it. A painted accent always sets TextColor; a rarity_through accent never does. There is no third case.
_rarity_through_rule.uniques_and_jewels: NOT A DEFECT, and not a choice either — closed. Your measurement is the argument for keeping them: 7 of 8 rows fall below 2:1 without their TextColor, and Uniques T2 lands at exactly 1.00:1 because its plate IS the unique orange. That is not an accident to correct; it is the design — on a painted accent the rarity signal moved to the PLATE, which is why the plate can be the rarity colour and the text still has to be readable. Rarity-through is for the accent whose plate is deliberately neutral. Do not re-choose those backgrounds.

_muted_is_authored.decision: accent.muted is an AUTHORED value, one per accent — not a formula. Your §1-3 are right and they are one problem, not three: the formula did not survive contact with either golden, and it is used in exactly two places.
_muted_is_authored.the_two_places: T3's PLATE and T4's TEXT — and they are now THE SAME VALUE. That is deliberate and it is the property that makes the tail cohere: the text at T4 is the colour of the plate two rungs above it.
_muted_is_authored.currency: 170 158 130 — Sharket's own authored tan, which is what reply 05 reverted T3 to. So no t3_bg override is needed: the literal you spotted IS accent.muted, it was just wearing a formula's name.
_muted_is_authored.essences: 140 152 178. The old golden's 146 156 178 was, as you worked out, a survivor of reply 03's retired 'muted lightened 0.25'. Discard it.
_muted_is_authored.what_this_retires: The lum / desaturate / darken chain from reply 03. Delete it — the arithmetic you recomputed was wrong (you are right about the blue channel) and there is nothing left that needs it.
_muted_is_authored.count: 24 values, one per accent, listed on each accent as `muted`. That takes the authored total to ~65 and it is worth it: every one is inspectable, and a wrong muted is visible on the board rather than emergent from a formula.

accents._about: 26 accents. solid + deep are the only authored colours; every T2/T3 plate is a transform of them. shape and beam are the icon/beam axis. icon_floor is the lowest rung drawing an icon. Below T3 the accent leaves the plate and survives as text.

currency.note: The house accent. Every other row is measured against this one.

fragments.note: Purple as the atlas shows it. Splinters are drop-disabled.

scarabs.note: Sharket's scarab green — near the atlas family without joining it.

div_cards.note: Widest value spread of any category; needs its own blue.

uniques.note: The one hue players read without being taught.

blight_oils.note: Held clear of currency orange so a Golden Oil is never a Divine.

fossils.note: Warm but darker than currency; resonators share it.

delirium.note: Grey-lilac, matching the orbs. ⚠️ MEASURED: buys exactly ONE base — Delirium Orb is ruthless_exclusive and the fifteen Standard variants are retired. Still worth it to make the orb unmistakable, but it is one line, not a family.

heist.note: Red accent, Pentagon shape, icon_floor T3. Heist is MAPLIKE: a contract is somewhere you go, so it never drops to the bulk rungs. See _heist_rule.

expedition.note: Logbooks and reroll currency. Maplike like heist — Pentagon, and a logbook is a destination too.

breach.note: Foulborn uniques and wombgifts only, since splinters are drop-disabled. Star, because a foulborn unique IS a unique — which is also what separates it from fragments' Hexagon. Same purple band as fragments, told apart by white text.

ritual.note: Blood, and far enough from Heist red that the shapes are not doing all the work.

jewels.note: Pink is otherwise unused, which makes a jewel drop unmistakable.

maps.note: TWO exceptions: plate follows item rarity, icon colour follows map tier. Floor drops to T3 so white maps keep an icon.

equipment.note: SUPERSEDED as a single accent — see gear_ladder.groups (armour, weapons, jewellery, flasks). Kept as the fallback for any gear category not in a group. shape stays null: gear is iconless below T0. ⚠️ After the equipment reshape this accent covers ONE category where it used to cover 23: Rare Equipment. The per-class hues did not survive the collapse and should not be reinvented there — see gear_ladder.groups.fallback.

tainted.note: SPLIT OFF currency at the designer's call — Tainted Mythic Orb was reading as ordinary currency at every rung. Keeps currency's Diamond, because it IS currency; the hue is vaal crimson, the colour corruption already wears in game. ⚠️ REVISED from an earlier 210 55 30: at 8° from heist and with a near-clone muted it failed the bar this bank sets for itself on the ritual card — 'far enough from Heist red that the shapes are not doing all the work'. At 340° it sits 11° off ritual, 20° off heist and 20° off jewels, all clear of the ≥6° rule, and at roughly twice ritual's luminance. Clears 5.17:1 on white, so no t0_text.

recipes.note: SPLIT OFF vendor at the designer's call. FilterBlade and Sharket both put a white-ish plate on 6-socket and RGB — it is the chromatic-recipe signal and players already read it. Vendor bulk stays grey for Legacy and Chancing; a recipe you can act on is not bulk. Moon comes out of reserve: recipes are the one iconless-by-inheritance category that genuinely wants findability on the ground.

vendor.note: Legacy and Chancing only — Vendor Recipes split off onto its own `recipes` accent. The noise floor as a category rather than a rung.

flasks.note: Life/Mana/Utility/Tinctures. Uses Raindrop — one of the four shapes held in reserve; a flask is not any of the other eight.

quest.note: Quest Items, Magic Net. Green is the game's own quest convention. Always visible regardless of strictness.

allflame.note: Curse of the Allflame, Enshrouding Crystals, Enshrouded Gear. Ember orange, clear of currency's yellow-orange.

corpses.note: Necropolis. A flesh tone, deliberately unlike anything tradeable. MEASURED: 114 bases in the 3.29 CN GGPK, 102 mapped across five rungs — real content.

gold.note: EXCEPTION: gold is auto-collected, so its label is a readout rather than a call to action. It never emits SetBackgroundColor at ANY rung — always the borderless form. No icon, no beam either.

state_borders._about: Rule deviations, border channel only, one Continue rule each. rank breaks ties when states stack — higher rank wins.

linked.note: ⚠️ SIX, not five. In Ruthless a 6-link is a chase drop and a 5-link is common enough to be noise — the author's own framing, and it is the right one. A 5-link gets NO state border: if it deserves attention it deserves a rung, which is a matching decision rather than a decoration.

state_borders._conditions: Thresholds, so none of these need guessing: corrupted = Corrupted True; influenced = HasInfluence any; fractured = FracturedItem True; enchanted = AnyEnchantment True; linked = LinkedSockets >= 6.

text_swaps._about: Properties that BEAT rarity take the text, freeing the border for real states. Own block, not a rule deviation. Five swaps now. The channel is the constant; the COLOUR is chosen per family for the plate it speaks against (see map_special.why_not_120_235_210).
text_swaps._never_on_t0_t1: See _swaps_never_paint_the_house_rungs. A swap needs a neutral plate to speak against. Note this is a FLOOR on the rung range, not the range itself — the range comes from what the block claims.

crafting.condition: block originates in Equipment/Crafting Priority.json AND asserts a property of the INSTANCE (percentile, quality, memory strands) — never the four ilvl bands, which assert a property of the base type
crafting.answer: YES — generalise. The swap channel already means 'this instance beats its rarity'; 'this base is worth crafting' is the same claim about the same item, so it takes the same colour rather than a 27th accent. Same value as quality (120 235 210) DELIBERATELY: they are one idea, and FilterBlade reaching 0 240 190 for the identical set of purposes independently is the corroboration.
crafting.what_this_costs: Crafting bases lose rarity-through at T2/T3 ONLY, not across the ladder. The four ilvl bands sit at T4/T5 and keep it. So the loss lands where you are going to scour the item anyway — the base, the ilvl and the roll are the signal — and the rarity channel survives untouched at the floor, where an i84 base's rarity IS the only thing distinguishing it. That split is the reason to take the swap rather than FilterBlade's whole-purpose version.
crafting.note: Fires on the BLOCK, not on a property threshold — 'this block is in Crafting Priority' is the condition. That is what separates it from quality, which fires on Quality >= 21 wherever that is true.
crafting.why_not_the_ilvl_bands: ⚠️ REVISED from 'T2-T3 only'. The rung range was always a PROXY for the real condition and the code side found where the proxy leaks: T4 is not the ilvl bands, it is the other half of the memory strands, and a memory strand is a claim about the instance — the exact sentence this swap exists to say. My own justification named 'the four ilvl bands', and those are T5. So the swap follows the CLAIM, not the rung: every property-asserting block takes it, the ilvl bands never do. Measured: 88 of the 90 residual identical-draw bases are claimed first by Strands T2, so this boundary was essentially the whole remainder.

quality.note: Scoped, NOT universal. Game already prints 'Superior' for 1-30; only 21-30 matters, and only on a base already worth showing — T0-T2. Never on T3 or below: quality does not rescue a base you would not have picked up.

thresholds._note: MEASURED: gem quality caps at 20, so 21 is not a breakpoint on a gem — 23 is, paired with GemLevel >= 21. Two entries, one rule. ⚠️ The operator needs a space before its value: 'Quality >= 21'; '>=21' is rejected by the game.

only_on_rungs: any — maps never wear a house plate, see _swaps_never_paint_the_house_rungs
map_special.condition: the block asserts a modifier or origin on a map that still has its own MapTier: influenced, Zana memory, enchanted, 8-mod corrupted, Elder, Shaper Guardian, Vaal Temple. NOT T17 (that is a tier, not a claim — it takes the top anchor and the swap fires on it only if it is also modified). NOT logbooks (no MapTier).
map_special.answer: SWAP, and it is forced rather than chosen. By the rule from reply 16 — a swap fires on blocks asserting a property of the INSTANCE — an influenced or enchanted or 8-mod map is exactly that claim. And an accent is now unavailable: the plate is spoken for by the tier, so an accent would take the plate and delete the tier. Text is the only free channel, which is what a swap is.
map_special.why_not_120_235_210: ⚠️ THIS IS THE GENERAL RULE, not a maps exception: a swap colour is chosen for THE PLATE IT SPEAKS AGAINST. The channel is the constant, never the hex. 120 235 210 measures 9.99:1 on gear's near-black plate and about 1.3:1 on a 242 map plate — the same colour, unusable. Maps run light, so the maps swap runs dark.
map_special.t17_falls_out: A T17 is top-of-ramp (255 255 255 plate) AND special (swap), so it renders deep violet on white — which is FilterBlade's 100 0 122-on-white 'top map' band, reached by construction rather than by copying. Their SECOND purple exists because their ramp does not reach white; ours does, so one authored value gives both looks.
map_special.collision_check: breach 160 45 255 and jewels 250 80 195 are both far brighter and neither shares a channel with this — they are plates, this is text on a light plate. Two purples in one filter is only a problem when they compete for the same surface.

text_swaps._states_can_be_redundant: ⚠️ A state is REDUNDANT when the block's own condition IS the state's condition, and it should be suppressed there. The 6-Link block matches LinkedSockets >= 6, which is exactly what the `linked` state asserts — so drawing the linked border on it spends the border to say what the whole block already is. Suppress it and the border stays free for `corrupted`, which a 6-link can also be and which is the one that would actually be news. This is the inverse of Fractured, where the border carries what the rung cannot; same principle read from the other end.

state_budget._about: MEASURED from emitted blocks by the code side, reply 03 — supersedes my earlier inference, which was low in three places.
state_budget._corrections: maps +influenced (all four conquerors matched today), jewels +enchanted (cluster jewels rank on EnchantmentPassiveNum), uniques +influenced (Elder/Shaper + synthesised). Consequence: maps, jewels and uniques all LOSE the T5-borderless form.

size_map._about: Shipped SEPARATELY from presets. Six rungs.
size_map._note: 30 is below the game's own 32 on purpose. No hide style: Ruthless draws Minimal, so a hidden block emits no style lines at all. ONE ramp for everything, gear included — see gear_ladder.gear_size_ramp for why Sharket's six-step gear ramp was declined.

goldens._about: Implement the transforms in rung_recipes, expand these two accents, and compare. Pure function, no I/O.

currency._note: Currency now uses T0-T4 and skips only T5 — it has no floor below scrolls. Sharket's tan is T3 and his scroll plate is T4, both untouched.

T4._note: Same value as T3's plate. Not a coincidence — see rung_recipes._muted_is_authored.

essences.rarity_through_note: Essences are always painted — rarity is meaningless on them.

open_questions: Icon floor per category (§4.1) — needs an in-game sweep. Legacy is the biggest single cut (17/17 draw an icon AND a beam on the vendor accent, whose floor is none); General is 48/43.
Fragments vs Breach in a real map: both purple, separated on text (black vs white) and shape (Hexagon vs Star). Author: 'fine for now.'
Gold auto-pickup confirmation in Ruthless — the whole plate: never exception rests on it.

Ward bases: COMPOSITION is the author's call (cross-class Ward concept vs split on item class). The look needs nothing either way — Expedition Ward-Bases already has its own accent rather than a gear group hue, which is the cross-class answer; if it splits, Iron Flask simply lands on the flasks accent. If it ever wants a ladder, its three ilvl bands (24-25 / 48-49 / 68-69) map to gear depth 3 = T2 T3 T4.

Campaign Safety Net / Aggressive Magic Hide points at a Tier 9 row Campaign does not have. It reads as a hide ('Hide Magic after Act 3') but is not flagged as one — flag it hide and it emits Minimal and needs no row. If it is genuinely meant to show, it is Campaign T5.

_text_brightness_ladder._about: Six rungs, T0-T5. Plate luminance falls monotonically; the accent appears on the plate only at T2/T3 and as text at T4.
_text_brightness_ladder.T5: accent.muted darkened .15 text, NO plate, dim accent border — the floor
_text_brightness_ladder.rule: Plate luminance strictly descends. Rarity-through drops the text and ranks on the same plates, border always free for states.

_category_exceptions._about: Seven. An exception substitutes one accent into a rung and never changes the rung's structure — except gold, maps and heist, which are noted. ⚠️ corrupted_tainted was RETIRED: tainted currency is now an ordinary accent (205 40 95) in the bank, not a structural exception, so it costs no exception at all. The old entry described the grey-plate treatment that split replaced.
_category_exceptions.currency: none needed — it IS the house ladder
_category_exceptions.gold: plate: never, at any rung. Auto-collected, so the label is informational. Closes Currency/Gold.json completely: no plate, no beam, no icon.
_category_exceptions.uniques: brown substitutes into the accent slot; the one gear family that paints its text
_category_exceptions.maps: plate = MAP TIER (see maps_tier_ramp) + icon colour from the same three bands + icon_floor T3. PAINTED, black text — no longer rarity_through, which also repairs the invariant. Still ONE exception, grown rather than added: it was always 'the plate is not the rung's' — now it says which axis takes it.
_category_exceptions.divination_cards: own blue — widest value spread of any category
_category_exceptions.heist: rung = area quality (handpicked list of nine); floor is T3, never the bulk rungs; Pentagon + icon_floor T3. Matching-side change; see _heist_rule.

_heist_rule._about: MEASURED FROM NEVERSINK (2026-08-03), and it is a structural idea rather than a colour one.
what_they_do: Contracts and blueprints are matched TOGETHER: Class == "Blueprints" "Contracts".
They sit under one waypoint labelled 'Maplike - contracts, logbooks, blueprints, memories' — heist is treated as map-like content, not as its own loot family.
The tier split is a HANDPICKED BaseType list, not a value ladder: $tier-?handpicked vs $tier-?any, plus an explicit Hide band ($tier-?exhide).
Their contract block draws MinimapIcon 0 Green Pentagon — size 0, the LARGEST icon the game has. Contracts are not treated as bulk in any sense.
_heist_rule.what_to_adopt: The rung is the AREA, and heist bottoms out at T3 — never T4 or T5. Handpicked area -> T2 (icon + Temp beam). Any other area -> T3 (icon, no beam). Excluded areas -> hidden, no style lines at all. A contract is somewhere you GO: the choice is which one to run, not whether it is worth picking up, so the bulk rungs do not apply to it.
_heist_rule.why_it_matters: Our heist ladder is two rungs deep and has no notion of which area is worth running — a Contract: Tunnels and a Contract: Cargo Hold look identical today. This is the single biggest legibility win available in the category, and it costs one BaseType list.
_heist_rule.implementation_note: This is a MATCHING change, not a theme change — it belongs on the rules axis per the rewrite doc, with the handpicked list as a rule's targets. The theme side only needs the T2/T4 presets it already has.
_heist_rule.open: Blueprints could sit one rung above contracts at the same area quality (a blueprint is the bigger commitment). Designer's call; NeverSink treats them alike.
_heist_rule.icon: Pentagon, taken out of reserve for maplike content (heist contracts and blueprints, expedition logbooks, memories). icon_floor T3 like maps, so every visible contract carries an icon — the point of the icon here is findability, not value.
_heist_rule.correction: ⚠️ Supersedes reply 07, which put non-handpicked areas at T4. That was wrong: T4 is the vendor-bulk rung and a contract is never bulk.
_heist_rule.measured_areas: Our tree already maps six of NeverSink's nine in one tier (Heist Contract T0): Smuggler's Den, Laboratory, Prohibited Library, Underbelly, Records Office, Mansion. Missing: Bunker, Repository, Tunnels. ⚠️ Heist/Blueprints.json has an EMPTY mapping — the blueprint ladder does not exist yet, so blueprints-above-contracts is new work either way.

_shape_reserve.note: Raindrop -> flasks, Pentagon -> maplike (heist, expedition), Moon -> vendor recipes. Tainted takes Diamond, shared with currency — same shape, different hue, which is the correct reading: tainted currency IS currency. One shape held for future league content. Wombgifts take Star with the rest of Breach, NOT Hexagon — Hexagon is atlas keys (fragments, scarabs, breachstones).

_q21_scope: T2 only. Narrowed from T0-T2 by _swaps_never_paint_the_house_rungs, and now stated in the array too (quality.only_on_rungs) rather than only in prose — the machine-readable field was the stale one, which is the exact inversion of 'follow the machine files'.
_swaps_never_paint_the_house_rungs: ⚠️ RESTATED — the rule is about the PLATE, not the rung's name. A text swap only fires where the plate is NEUTRAL, i.e. where the plate is a house recipe (T0's white, T1's red) whose own colour is already the whole signal. Overwriting that with a quieter text is the thing being forbidden. It was written as 'never on T0 or T1' because until maps, rung and plate were the same thing — every rung supplied its own plate, so naming the rung named the plate. MAPS BREAK THAT IDENTITY: their plate comes from maps_tier_ramp at every rung, so no map ever wears a house plate and the precondition never obtains. A special map is therefore swap-eligible at ANY rung, including T1, and the deadlock the code side found dissolves without weakening the rule anywhere else. Where rung and plate are still the same thing — every accent except maps — nothing changes.

flat_look._about: A look OFF the ladder, for categories that have no tiers because ranking them is a category error. Author's call: 'special items like quest could have its own theme, they usually have no tiers.'
flat_look.why_a_bright_border: Two markers, one per form. PAINTED (zero-state classes): a border at FULL accent strength — no rung sets one there, T5's is deliberately dim. GEAR: plate alpha 255, just above the ladder's 250. Neither spends a channel a state needs.
flat_look.legality: Painted form: state_budget[class] must be empty — true for all four entries. Gear form: no legality test needed, because it spends nothing. That is why it is the safer shape.
flat_look.does_not_apply_to: Not every one-rung category is flat. Legacy and Chancing have one rung because they are BULK, and bulk is a rank — they stay on the ladder at T5. Flat is for utility.
flat_look.implementation: A block sets flat: true instead of a rung. The compiler emits the recipe above and skips the rung lookup entirely — so rung_by_depth is not consulted for these categories.

recipe_rarity_through._why: YOUR SUGGESTION, adopted — it is better than mine. The gear ladder runs plate alpha 250/240/230/220/210, so alpha 255 is unused and sits just outside it: full opacity reads as 'off the ladder' without spending a channel, and it leaves the border alone so every state border still composes.

flat_look.icon_disambiguation: Flat draws '1 White <shape>' and the maps exception draws '1 White Square' for white-tier maps — same colour, two meanings. SHAPE disambiguates: Square is a map, any other shape at 1 White is unranked. Encode it that way rather than treating White as a single semantic.
flat_look.validator: Errors to assert: (1) a flat PAINTED block on a class whose state_budget is non-empty; (2) any flat block that emits SetTextColor on a gear-accent category; (3) any flat block emitting a MinimapIcon where the accent's shape is null.
flat_look.removed: Magic Net is now a 4-rung AreaLevel band over magic gear — a ladder, and a gear one, so it moved off the quest accent onto equipment with its own override. Stygian Vise has 2 rungs and is a judgement call; left OFF the flat list for now since two rungs is a rank.
flat_look.caution: ⚠️ Relics: 7 of its 14 GGPK bases are [DO NOT USE] and our category holds one. Enshrouded Gear's bases are not in the dump yet. Both stay on the gear form, which is safe by construction — a spurious plate is cosmetic, and there is no border to be spurious about.

gear_ladder._about: Sharket's COLOURS on a plate-ranked ladder. His structure (rung on the border) was measured unbuildable — see border_is_unavailable.

what_sharket_does.T0: text #ffffff, border #ffffff, plate #8296af (the class hue), PlayEffect Grey, MinimapIcon 0 Grey Star
what_sharket_does.T1: text #ffffff, border #8296af, plate #1a1e23, PlayEffect Grey, MinimapIcon 1 Grey Diamond
what_sharket_does.T2: text #95a6bb, border #8296af, plate #101016, MinimapIcon 1 Grey Circle
what_sharket_does.Tier9: 18px, text #5a5a64aa, border #2d2d3478, plate transparent — a 'shown but nearly gone' band
what_sharket_does.sizes: 45 / 42 / 39 / 36 / 34 / 31 / 18 — six distinct steps, not shared ones

what_we_take: The group hues, Sharket's steel blue verbatim for armour.
The plate as gear's ranking channel, darkening as the rung falls.

T0's treatment: NOT taken. ⚠️ RESOLVED — T0 takes the HOUSE rung on gear like every other family, per rung_recipes.T0.rarity_through. Sharket's white-on-group-hue was authored against a mid-dark steel blue; reply 14 flattened gear to the neutral 170 170 170 fallback and turned the same recipe into white-on-light-grey at 2.32:1, on the one rung whose job is drop everything. It had never rendered because no equipment category had a T0 until the crafting promotion created one.
Icons at T0 only (0 White Star). Nothing below.
gear_ladder.what_we_change: He paints gear TEXT in the class hue, which overrides rarity — the most valuable thing on a gear label. We put the hue on the PLATE and hand the text back to the game.
gear_ladder.what_we_decline: Tier 9 at 18px (a hidden block emits nothing here). His six-step size ramp — gear uses the shared 45/45/40/35/35/30. And his transparent T4/T5 plates: with the border unavailable, the plate is the ONLY rung channel gear has, so it can never reach zero.
gear_ladder.gear_size_ramp: DECLINED. Sharket runs gear on 45/42/39/36/34/31 (six distinct steps). Author's call: gear uses the shared 45/45/40/35/35/30 like everything else. The reasoning holds up — the border is already carrying the rung on gear, so size does not need to repeat it, and one ramp of four values is easier for a player to retune than two ramps of ten.

armour.covers: class_hierarchy equipment/armour — body armours, boots, gloves, helmets, shields, quivers

jewellery.covers: class_hierarchy equipment/jewellery — rings, amulets, belts. NOT trinkets.

fallback.covers: genuinely mixed-class categories: Rare Equipment, Fractured, Influenced, Crafting Bases, Magic Net, Heist Experimented, Uniques, Legacy
fallback._campaign_is_not_here_any_more: Campaign's four files split BY CLASS (10 Weapon / 20 Armour / 30 Jewellery / 40 Flask), so group_resolution resolves them to weapons, armour, jewellery and flasks with no hand-mapping. Campaign is where the gear family distinction now lives.
fallback._rare_equipment: The 23 per-class categories collapsed into one mixed file, so one hue is the honest answer there. Armour's 130 150 175 winning that merge was an accident of coverage, not a decision — use the fallback grey.

gear_ladder._why_four: Sharket has ~30 class hues, which is the variance the author asked to cut. One shared grey was my over-correction. Four groups answers the only question a gear drop poses at distance — weapon or chest — without 30 colours to learn.

states_take_the_border.problem: Gear now spends the border on the rung, and gear is the class that holds all five state borders.
states_take_the_border.resolution: The state WINS the border and the plate steps down one step to compensate. This is not a new invention — it is the designer's own 'enhanced' escalation as recorded in theme-pipeline-rewrite.md ('state hue takes the border, plate steps down'), so the vocabulary already exists on both sides.
states_take_the_border.consequence: On a stateful gear item the rung is carried by SIZE and the plate alone. That is acceptable: knowing an item is corrupted matters more than knowing it is T3 rather than T4.
states_take_the_border.validator: A gear block that emits both a rung border and a state border is an error — exactly one must win, and it is the state.

gear_ladder.icons: ⚠️ GEAR IS ICONLESS except T0, which draws '0 White Star' by the existing chase rule (a chase drop takes Star whatever its class). No group declares a shape, so no other rung can emit an icon line — do not attempt <group.shape>, it does not exist. Sharket draws icons at T0-T2 (0 Grey Star / 1 Grey Diamond / 1 Grey Circle); we decline T1 and T2 because his shapes vary by RUNG, which collides with shape = class everywhere else in this system.

border_is_unavailable.finding: MEASURED BY THE CODE SIDE, reply 03. A block without Continue terminates matching, so decorators MUST emit before the content blocks; Continue then hands every channel the later block sets to that later block. A gear rung on the border would therefore overwrite the state border on the class holding the most states.
border_is_unavailable.evidence: 525 of 529 blocks after the state decorator already set their own SetBorderColor on today's tree — the state border is being eaten almost everywhere right now.
border_is_unavailable.consequence: 'The border is free on every rung' is not a stylistic preference. It is a build constraint of the one-pass model, and it holds with NO exception, gear included.
border_is_unavailable.rejected_alternative: Emitting gear blocks WITH Continue so a later decorator wins — then every later matching block layers on too, including the final show-all net, which would repaint the gear it was meant to catch.

gear_ladder.group_resolution: DERIVED, not hand-mapped: GGPK BaseItemTypes.ItemClassesKey -> ItemClasses.Name -> class_hierarchy.yaml intermediate node. 33 of 41 gear-bearing categories resolve to one group with no judgement. Do NOT use _meta.item_class — it is a display label ('Breach Grasping Mail', 'Crafting Priority'), not a game class.
gear_ladder.not_gear: Measured: Trinkets, Relics and Heist Equipment are NOT gear — own classes under misc/league_content. They do not take a group hue.
gear_ladder.flasks: NOT a gear group. class_hierarchy has flasks as its own top-level node, and it holds only identified/corrupted/mirrored — one state, not five. Keeps its own accent.
gear_ladder._t1_stays_on_the_ladder: ⚠️ THE ANSWER TO 'T0 and T1, or T0 only': T0 only. T1 keeps the gear ladder, and the code side was right not to change it on the strength of a document disagreeing with itself. The principle, so this does not need re-deciding: T0 is CATEGORICAL — 'nothing else on this screen matters' is a claim about the whole drop, so it must render identically in every family or the claim does not survive being read. T1 is RELATIVE — 'the top of this category' is a claim about the family, so it renders in the family's own vocabulary. That is why the argument that forces T0 stops at T1, and it is why Campaign T1 keeps its dark plate: a good act-3 upgrade is not a Divine Orb and must not wear its colour.

icon_floor_sweep._about: Measured icon counts per category (ruthless/soft, 526 Show blocks), from the code side.
icon_floor_sweep.start_here: General 48 blocks / 43 icons, and Map Fragments 42 / 19 — where a floor either pays or spams.
icon_floor_sweep.biggest_subtraction: ⚠️ Legacy draws an icon AND a beam on all 17 of its blocks. On the vendor accent with icon_floor: none that is the single biggest removal in the sweep.
icon_floor_sweep.no_vocabulary_to_preserve: The current filter has 15 distinct icon values but 245 of 285 are just two — '1 White Diamond' (123) and '0 White Star' (122). The nine-shape vocabulary replaces nothing.

rung_by_depth._moved: ⚠️ THIS TABLE NOW LIVES IN accent-category-map.json AND ONLY THERE. Two copies existed and they disagreed at depth 3; the map's copy was the only one with a gear template and the file overrides, so it is primary. Do not restore a copy here — a second copy is how they drifted.
rung_by_depth._why_it_matters: Its absence is what compiled Legacy and Chancing to T2 — the money plate with a Temp beam — on bulk. If a category's rungs come out loud and wrong, this table is the first thing to check.
rung_by_depth._depth3: Resolved to T1 T2 T4. T3 is the muted accent plate and only means something below the full-strength T2; with one accent rung there is nothing for it to be muted against, so a 3-deep ladder would name its family more weakly than a 2-deep one. Recorded as an invariant, not a preference: see _invariants.painted_t3_needs_t2 in the map.

maps_tier_ramp._about: ⚠️ NEW, and it is the answer to reply 09 §2.1: YES, maps take the tier on the PLATE. Not 16 authored values — 7 anchors, and the compile interpolates the rest. Same authored-vs-derived split as everything else in this kit.
maps_tier_ramp._why: Everywhere else a rung answers 'how much do I care?', and two tiers can honestly share one answer. On a map the tier IS the item's identity — it sets monster level, atlas progression and price, and it is the one number read before deciding to run it. Sixteen values in two steps is not compression, it is the information being dropped. Same shape as the crafting problem one level up: the ladder ranks HOW GOOD, and what needs saying is WHICH ONE.
maps_tier_ramp._anchors_are_the_atlas_bands: The three anchors are white / yellow / red — the player's own model, and the same bands the icon colour already uses. So icon and plate now say the same thing at two distances: the icon on the minimap, the plate on the ground. Band at a glance, tier on a look.
maps_tier_ramp.interpolate: linear in sRGB between the bracketing anchors, per MapTier. T2-T4 from T1/T5, T7-T9 from T6/T10, T12-T15 from T11/T16.
maps_tier_ramp.monotonic: Luminance ascends with tier and never doubles back — 110 → 146 → 150 → 200 → 210 → 242 → 255 — so _plate_rule holds unchanged. The band TINT (neutral / warm / warm-red) is what makes the band readable without counting steps; luminance is what makes the tier readable.
maps_tier_ramp.text: 0 0 0 throughout. Black on the darkest anchor is 4.3:1 at 45px.
maps_tier_ramp.⚠️_maps_stops_being_rarity_through: REQUIRED, and it fixes a contradiction that was already in this kit: _invariants.rarity_through_is_an_accent_property says 'only the equipment accent has it', while _category_exceptions.maps said maps were rarity_through too. The plate ramp forces the issue the right way — the game's white Normal-map text on a 242 plate is unreadable, so maps must paint. Only equipment is rarity_through now, exactly as the invariant always said.
maps_tier_ramp.what_the_rung_still_owns: Size, icon size, icon colour and beam. The rung is NOT retired for maps — only its plate is overridden. This is the same decoupling the standard already sells: rung = how much I care, and now for maps only, plate = which one it is.
maps_tier_ramp.override_status: Maps/Base Maps.json (5) T1 T2 T2 T3 T3 stays as the SIZE ladder and is no longer a plate ladder. The doubling that collapsed red into T16 and yellow into white is harmless once the plate carries the tier.
maps_tier_ramp.special_map_rung: ⚠️ ANSWER to reply 10 §1.1: NOT a fixed T2. A special map takes ITS OWN BAND'S RUNG, floored at T2 — whichever is louder. Flat T2 has a bug in it: a T16 influenced map would sit at 40px while the same map unmodified sits at 45px, so adding a modifier would make an item QUIETER. The floor is what T2 is for (an influenced T3 is worth picking up even though a plain T3 is not); the band rung is what stops the floor from becoming a ceiling. General form, worth keeping: a claim about an instance may raise an item's rung and must never lower it.
maps_tier_ramp.t17_and_vaal_temple: ⚠️ ANSWER to §1.2: BOTH GO ON THE RAMP, and yes — that is the theme telling the matching side to delete a rule. Stated as a decision, as you asked. A T17 on the house red plate loses its tier, which is the exact failure this whole exception exists to prevent; I wrote that a Vaal Temple T16 must not stop being a T16, and a T17 on red stops being a T17. And the ramp is not the quieter option: its top anchor is 255 255 255, the loudest plate in the system — T17 lands white plate, violet swap text, 45px, Red Square, beam. Louder than the house red, and it still says which tier it is. Vaal Temple >= 16 is a special like any other: tier plate, swap text, band rung.
maps_tier_ramp.no_map_wears_a_house_plate: The honest scope of this exception, now that it is settled: maps opt out of the house PLATES entirely, T0 through T5. Every map plate comes from the ramp. They keep the house SIZES, icons and beams. That is the whole of it — one exception, and this is its edge.
maps_tier_ramp.icon_bands: ⚠️ ANSWER to §3: YES, build it, on the same rules as the plate. Three values, not sixteen — Red for T11-17, Yellow for T6-10, White for T1-5. The point of banding plate and icon together is that what a map says on the ground and what it says on the minimap cannot disagree; one icon colour for sixteen tiers is the minimap half going silent. Cheap, and it is the reason the anchors are the atlas bands rather than an even ramp.
maps_tier_ramp.logbooks_are_not_maps: ⚠️ ANSWER to §1.3: they leave the maps accent entirely, for the reason you gave — no MapTier means the ramp has nothing to say and the swap has no plate to speak against. They go to the EXPEDITION accent, which already covers them ('logbooks and reroll currency, maplike, so Pentagon too') and was only ever missing them by historical accident: they sat in the maps tier when that tier meant 'special things', and it now means 'maps with a claim'. The enchanted logbook is not a second tier — it is the ENCHANTED STATE on the same block, which is the state channel doing its job exactly as it does for Fractured.

_icon_floor_is_a_grant: ⚠️ ANSWER to reply 11 §3, and a clarification of a mechanism rather than a new one. icon_floor GRANTS an icon down to the named rung; it does not merely gate a recipe that has already declined to draw one. rung_recipes.T3.icon is null as the DEFAULT — 'below the floor by default' — and a category whose icon_floor is T3 overrides that default and draws. Maps are the case it was written for: 'maps drop their floor to T3, because a white map is a real decision while you are progressing'. So the bands are Red T11-17 / Yellow T6-10 / White T1-5, all drawn, with SIZE from the rung (0 at T0/T1, 1 at T2, 2 at T3) and COLOUR from the band. If the floor were a gate, no category could ever be granted an icon the rung ladder had refused, and the per-category floor would have nothing to do.
_overrides_are_written_against_contents: ⚠️ THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE PATTERN, named so it stops recurring: an override written against a category's NAME rather than its CONTENTS. Chancing (repathed — the name said currency, the file lives under vendor recipes), Magic Net (annotated (4) for a shape it did not have), and now Vendor Recipes, whose file is not vendor recipes at all — it is sockets, colours and links. The rule: an override must be justified by what the file HOLDS, and the justification belongs in its note. A note that only restates the category name is the tell.
